correctness.rationale: Theorem 1.7 of arXiv:2610.00130v1 applies because d=rm>W=n+1+m, gcd(d,W)=1, smooth branch implies quasismoothness, and r,m>=2 exclude a linear cone. A graded automorphism in weights (1^{n+1},m) has x->Lx and z->az+h_m(x); comparing the z^{r-1} coefficient forces h_m=0, then the constant term gives G(Lx)=a^r F(x). This proves both branch-divisor projective equivalence and cover isomorphism over the induced base map.

value.rationale: The branch divisor and covering projection are natural geometric data of a cyclic cover and are not automatically preserved by an arbitrary graded coordinate change. The exact z^{r-1}-coefficient argument removes the full degree-m translation ambiguity in the cover coordinate, upgrading the new general-type weighted-hypersurface reconstruction theorem to reconstruction of the covering structure uniformly for every cyclic degree r>=2 under explicit arithmetic hypotheses. This extends the source's branch-recovery phenomenon beyond its Fano double-cover corollary to a broad natural general-type family.
